{
  "findings": [

      "title": "Password verification is skipped whenever a TOTP code is present, enabling second-factor-only login",
      "body": "In the credentials authorize function, the password is only verified when credentials.totpCode is absent. The new backup-code branch is selected whenever credentials.backupCode is present, even if credentials.totpCode is also present. As a result, a CAL user with a password can authenticate with only a valid TOTP code, and a valid backup code plus any non-empty totpCode also bypasses password verification. This defeats the first authentication factor for 2FA logins. Password verification should be required for accounts that have a password, especially for backup-code use, instead of being skipped whenever totpCode is present."

    {
      "file": "packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts",
      "line": 149,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing reuse or resurrection of used codes",
      "body": "During login, the encrypted backup-code array is read, a matching index is set to null, and the user row is updated in a separate write. Concurrent successful logins can both read the same unused backup code before either update completes, allowing the same one-time code to be used more than once. Concurrent use of different codes can also cause last-write-wins to overwrite another request's nulling, effectively resurrecting a used code. This breaks the one-time-use guarantee. Use a transaction or an atomic/conditional update when consuming a backup code."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts",
      "line": 113,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Backup-code login is blocked for non-CAL identity-provider accounts",
      "body": "The early checks for non-CAL identity providers only exempt credentials.totpCode, not credentials.backupCode. If a user with 2FA enabled has a non-CAL identity provider (for example after identity-provider conversion/linking), supplying a backup code without a TOTP code throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled or IncorrectEmailPassword. The disable endpoint supports backup codes, but the login flow effectively makes backup recovery unavailable for these accounts. The checks should also allow backupCode where appropriate."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx",
      "line": 166,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Successful 2FA enable is not propagated if the modal is dismissed without clicking the explicit Close button",
      "body": "After the TOTP code is accepted, the modal moves to the backup-code screen and only calls onEnable when the user clicks the explicit Close button. If the dialog is dismissed through onOpenChange, such as ESC, backdrop click, or a parent-controlled close, onEnable is not called and the modal state is not reset. The settings screen can remain showing 2FA as disabled even though it is enabled on the server, and reopening the modal may show a stale step. The modal should handle close/dismiss by resetting state and notifying the parent appropriately."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx",
      "line": 71,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "resetState does not clear form values or sensitive generated 2FA state",
      "body": "resetState clears only password, error message, and step. It leaves the react-hook-form totpCode value, backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, and secret in state. A stale six-digit totpCode can trigger the auto-submit effect again if the modal is remounted or revisited, and stale QR/backup-code state can be shown unexpectedly. It also retains the blob URL containing backup codes. resetState should call form.reset(), clear all generated 2FA state, and revoke the object URL."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts",
      "line": 53,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "E2E assertion checks a Promise instead of the actual checked state",
      "body": "The test uses await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy(). locator.isChecked() returns a Promise, and asserting that the Promise is truthy does not verify that the switch is actually checked. This can pass even when 2FA was not enabled. The test also does not handle the new backup-code screen in this first flow. Use a web-first assertion such as toBeChecked() and handle the backup-code dialog."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts",
      "line": 12,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No E2E coverage for backup-code login or one-time consumption",
      "body": "The PR adds backup-code login and consumes backup codes on use, but the E2E tests only verify that backup codes are displayed, copied, and downloaded during setup. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, verifies that a used backup code is rejected, or disables 2FA using a backup code. The TODO in the test file acknowledges this gap. These flows should be covered before merge."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts",
      "line": 144,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Backup-code normalization only strips dashes",
      "body": "The backup-code check removes dashes with replaceAll('-', '') but does not trim whitespace or normalize letter case. Generated codes are lowercase hexadecimal strings. If a user copies a code with surrounding whitespace or uppercase characters, a valid code will be rejected. The same normalization issue exists in the disable endpoint. Trim and lowercase user input before comparison."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx",
      "line": 188,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Backup code can be submitted empty despite the input being marked required",
      "body": "The login form uses noValidate and the Zod schema only validates email/password while passing through other fields. When the user switches to the lost-access backup-code screen, the BackupCode input's required attribute is not enforced and there is no schema validation for backupCode. Submitting an empty backup code sends an empty value to the server, which then falls back to the TOTP path and returns a confusing second-factor-required error. Add validation for backupCode or avoid disabling native validation for this field."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx",
      "line": 278,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Copy button shows success even if clipboard write fails",
      "body": "The copy handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText without awaiting it or catching errors, then immediately shows a success toast. If the Clipboard API is unavailable, permission is denied, or the write rejects, the user still sees a success message, and an unhandled rejection may occur. Await the clipboard operation and show success only when it actually succeeds."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx",
      "line": 99,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Backup-code blob URL is not revoked on close or unmount",
      "body": "The component creates an object URL containing the user's backup codes for download. It only revokes a previous URL when a new setup response is received. If the modal is closed, cancelled, or the component unmounts, the object URL remains alive for the page lifetime, unnecessarily retaining sensitive backup-code data in memory. Revoke the object URL during reset/cleanup."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx",
      "line": 38,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Disable-2FA modal state persists when closed via dialog controls",
      "body": "The modal does not reset twoFactorLostAccess, form values, or error message when the dialog is closed through onOpenChange rather than through Cancel or successful disable. If a user opens the lost-access view, closes the modal, and reopens it, the modal can unexpectedly remain in lost-access mode or retain stale input/error state. Reset modal state when the dialog is closed or reopened."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Password verification is skipped whenever a TOTP code is present, enabling second-factor-only login
findings.body: In the credentials authorize function, the password is only verified when credentials.totpCode is absent. The new backup-code branch is selected whenever credentials.backupCode is present, even if credentials.totpCode is also present. As a result, a CAL user with a password can authenticate with only a valid TOTP code, and a valid backup code plus any non-empty totpCode also bypasses password verification. This defeats the first authentication factor for 2FA logins. Password verification should be required for accounts that have a password, especially for backup-code use, instead of being skipped whenever totpCode is present.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing reuse or resurrection of used codes
findings.body: During login, the encrypted backup-code array is read, a matching index is set to null, and the user row is updated in a separate write. Concurrent successful logins can both read the same unused backup code before either update completes, allowing the same one-time code to be used more than once. Concurrent use of different codes can also cause last-write-wins to overwrite another request's nulling, effectively resurrecting a used code. This breaks the one-time-use guarantee. Use a transaction or an atomic/conditional update when consuming a backup code.

findings.title: Backup-code login is blocked for non-CAL identity-provider accounts
findings.body: The early checks for non-CAL identity providers only exempt credentials.totpCode, not credentials.backupCode. If a user with 2FA enabled has a non-CAL identity provider (for example after identity-provider conversion/linking), supplying a backup code without a TOTP code throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled or IncorrectEmailPassword. The disable endpoint supports backup codes, but the login flow effectively makes backup recovery unavailable for these accounts. The checks should also allow backupCode where appropriate.

findings.title: Successful 2FA enable is not propagated if the modal is dismissed without clicking the explicit Close button
findings.body: After the TOTP code is accepted, the modal moves to the backup-code screen and only calls onEnable when the user clicks the explicit Close button. If the dialog is dismissed through onOpenChange, such as ESC, backdrop click, or a parent-controlled close, onEnable is not called and the modal state is not reset. The settings screen can remain showing 2FA as disabled even though it is enabled on the server, and reopening the modal may show a stale step. The modal should handle close/dismiss by resetting state and notifying the parent appropriately.

findings.title: resetState does not clear form values or sensitive generated 2FA state
findings.body: resetState clears only password, error message, and step. It leaves the react-hook-form totpCode value, backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, and secret in state. A stale six-digit totpCode can trigger the auto-submit effect again if the modal is remounted or revisited, and stale QR/backup-code state can be shown unexpectedly. It also retains the blob URL containing backup codes. resetState should call form.reset(), clear all generated 2FA state, and revoke the object URL.

findings.title: E2E assertion checks a Promise instead of the actual checked state
findings.body: The test uses await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy(). locator.isChecked() returns a Promise, and asserting that the Promise is truthy does not verify that the switch is actually checked. This can pass even when 2FA was not enabled. The test also does not handle the new backup-code screen in this first flow. Use a web-first assertion such as toBeChecked() and handle the backup-code dialog.

findings.title: No E2E coverage for backup-code login or one-time consumption
findings.body: The PR adds backup-code login and consumes backup codes on use, but the E2E tests only verify that backup codes are displayed, copied, and downloaded during setup. There is no test that logs in with a backup code, verifies that a used backup code is rejected, or disables 2FA using a backup code. The TODO in the test file acknowledges this gap. These flows should be covered before merge.

findings.title: Backup-code normalization only strips dashes
findings.body: The backup-code check removes dashes with replaceAll('-', '') but does not trim whitespace or normalize letter case. Generated codes are lowercase hexadecimal strings. If a user copies a code with surrounding whitespace or uppercase characters, a valid code will be rejected. The same normalization issue exists in the disable endpoint. Trim and lowercase user input before comparison.

findings.title: Backup code can be submitted empty despite the input being marked required
findings.body: The login form uses noValidate and the Zod schema only validates email/password while passing through other fields. When the user switches to the lost-access backup-code screen, the BackupCode input's required attribute is not enforced and there is no schema validation for backupCode. Submitting an empty backup code sends an empty value to the server, which then falls back to the TOTP path and returns a confusing second-factor-required error. Add validation for backupCode or avoid disabling native validation for this field.

findings.title: Copy button shows success even if clipboard write fails
findings.body: The copy handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText without awaiting it or catching errors, then immediately shows a success toast. If the Clipboard API is unavailable, permission is denied, or the write rejects, the user still sees a success message, and an unhandled rejection may occur. Await the clipboard operation and show success only when it actually succeeds.

findings.title: Backup-code blob URL is not revoked on close or unmount
findings.body: The component creates an object URL containing the user's backup codes for download. It only revokes a previous URL when a new setup response is received. If the modal is closed, cancelled, or the component unmounts, the object URL remains alive for the page lifetime, unnecessarily retaining sensitive backup-code data in memory. Revoke the object URL during reset/cleanup.

findings.title: Disable-2FA modal state persists when closed via dialog controls
findings.body: The modal does not reset twoFactorLostAccess, form values, or error message when the dialog is closed through onOpenChange rather than through Cancel or successful disable. If a user opens the lost-access view, closes the modal, and reopens it, the modal can unexpectedly remain in lost-access mode or retain stale input/error state. Reset modal state when the dialog is closed or reopened.
